svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.23.4.3 Steel Beams
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.23 WOOD-FRAME CONSTRUCTION
Steel Beams

g.text: Joists bear on the top flange at
19 mm × 38 mm strips nailed to the joists
on both sides, against the flange (Note)
Steel floor beam with a laterally supported top flange
TABLE 9.23.4.3., MAXIMUM SPANS FOR STEEL BEAMS SUPPORTING FLOORS IN DWELLING UNITS, M
Supported joist length, m (half the sum of joist spans on both sides of the beam)
Notes to Table 9.23.4.3.: (1) See Note A-Table 9.23.4.3.

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
The spans for steel floor beams with laterally
supported top flanges conform to Table
These beams at least meet the requirements for
Grade 350 W steel in CSA G40.21, "Structural
quality steel."
A beam may be taken as laterally supported where
wood joists bear on its top flange at 600 mm or
less over its whole length, all the load comes
through the joists, and 19 mm × 38 mm wood strips
against the top flange are nailed on both sides
to the bottom of the joists. Other positive
lateral supports are acceptable. Straight-line
interpolation may be used between supported joist
lengths.
Drawn: beam shape and joist sizes are illustration only, joists at 400 mm o.c. Table values as printed.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.23.4.3. (page 9-174)
